articles.title: Robert Downey Jr. and Pedro Pascal Swap Places for Halloween With Mister Fantastic and Doctor Doom Costumes
articles.summary: Halloween had no shortage of viral costumes, but Robert Downey Jr. and Pedro Pascal might have taken the crown by swapping places as Mister Fantastic and Doctor Doom. Downey Jr.
body: Downey Jr. set Marvel feeds on fire late last night when he posted video of him and Pascal sharing their night dressed as their characters in next month's Avengers: Doomsday. Instead of playing Victor von Doom, though, he dressed up in Reed Richards' retro-themed blue outfit, with Pascal dropping his superhero attire to sport Doom's iconic metal mask.

It looks like Downey put a bit more effort into his Halloween costume, considering Pascal is wearing jeans and a sweatshirt, but the effect is still there. Finding a convincing replacement for Doctor Doom's magical get-up probably would have been more trouble than it's worth anyway. You can see Downey's video below.

They're the variants no one expected to see, but still the ones they got this Halloween. With Doomsday now just weeks away, we'll likely only see its many, many stars taking to social media to spread the word.

articles.title: 6 Perfect Star Trek Episodes to Watch to Say Goodbye to Patrick Stewart
articles.summary: Even more significant than the quantity of Star Trek that Stewart made was the quality. Kirk is in many ways a classic pulp action hero. He faces conflicts head on, never afraid to throw a punch or flirt with a sexy alien.
body: Star Trek wouldn’t be the cultural phenomenon it is today without Patrick Stewart. Sure, William Shatner launched the franchise by playing the USS Enterprise Captain James T. Kirk in 79 episodes. But Stewart led the United Federation of Planets’ flagship as Captain Jean-Luc Picard in 178 episodes over seven seasons of Star Trek: The Next Generation, and then returned to the role for 30 more episodes in Star Trek: Picard.

Any list of Stewart’s best episodes will closely mirror a general list of TNG ’s best moments. Stewart brought incredible gravitas to the show’s most emotionally brutal scenes and gentle humor to its silliest scenarios. Stewart’s death is devastating, but TNG already taught fans how to deal with loss and embrace the best parts of life. Celebrate Stewart by reliving some of his finest moments in TNG ’s six best Picard episodes.

articles.title: Doom Creator John Romero Revives Xbox-Canceled Game At New Publisher
articles.summary: The fate of the next game from Doom creator John Romero was in jeopardy after Xbox canceled the project last year. Thankfully, Romero confirmed in a new interview that the project will see the light of day, as his studio has found another publisher.
body: John Romero and his wife, game designer Brenda Romero, founded Romero Games over a decade ago and have made Gunman Taco Truck, Empire of Sin, and Sigil episodes in Doom + Doom II. The studio planned to make the jump to AAA shooter development with help from Xbox Game Studios, but Xbox dropped the project during its mass layoffs in 2025. Romero Games had to lay off more of its developers in turn.

In a recent interview with Video Games Chronicle, John Romero revealed more about the project's journey and confirmed that he was finally able to rehire some of the developers he had to lay off. Romero Games downscaled from 110 developers to just 5 initially, as they couldn't find funding. They still owned all the IP related to the project and eventually found someone to pick it back up.

"I just contacted somebody that I knew, and we basically did a deal, and so we have a new publisher," Romero revealed before admitting he "can't say anything about who it is, or when the announce is, or any of that stuff."
points: The fate of the next game from Doom creator John Romero was in jeopardy after Xbox canceled the project last year.
Thankfully, Romero confirmed in a new interview that the project will see the light of day, as his studio has found another publisher.

articles.title: Everyone Is Running a Con in You Can See Everything
articles.summary: Everyone is running a con in the Elizabeth Holmes Documentary You Can See Everything.
body: Full spoilers follow for You Can See Everything, which is in theaters now.

You Can See Everything is, deservedly, one of the most-talked-about films of the year, and is sailing past box office records for documentaries. The filmmaking itself is impressive, often surprising, and effective. But the movie’s staying power is as a social experiment about whether any of us truly know, care about, or communicate what’s “real” outside of our own interests. Truth exists on a spectrum in the world of this film, and it often feels like a game of narcissistic whack-a-mole.

We understand that co-directors Nathan Fielder (Nathan for You) and Lance Oppenheim (Primetime) haven’t delivered a definitive take on whether Elizabeth Holmes is a liar; according to the legal system and whistleblowers, she is, after her company Theranos was revealed to be, essentially, hawking a blood-testing machine that didn’t actually work. What the film is asking is whether Holmes understands that she is lying, or if she can discern the difference between what she wishes were so, and what is. It’s like crafting a “not guilty by reason of insanity” defense for fraud.
points: Everyone is running a con in the Elizabeth Holmes Documentary You Can See Everything.
Full spoilers follow for You Can See Everything, which is in theaters now.
You Can See Everything is, deservedly, one of the most-talked-about films of the year, and is sailing past box office records for documentaries.

articles.title: A Persona 1 Remake Is In Development, New Leak Suggests
articles.summary: Persona 4 Revival and Persona 6 aren't even out yet, and another Persona game has already leaked. Fittingly for Halloween, some new footage of an in-development Persona remake emerged online. It appears to be for a remake of Revelations: Persona, the first game in the series.
body: As Persona Central reported, about two minutes of gameplay for the remake emerged online on Halloween. Having watched the footage, it shows the first game's protagonist exploring a school-themed dungeon before entering combat. Tatsuya Suou, the protagonist of Persona 2: Innocent Sin, also appears. The video seems to have been made for an internal presentation, and fans have noticed it reuses some animations from Persona 4 Revival.

If this is real, this remake is likely still several years away from release. I wouldn't expect it to come out until after both Persona 4 Revival, which launches in Feb. 2027, and Persona 6, which does not have a release date. Regardless, this leaked footage suggests Atlus was happy with the response to Persona 3 Reload and wants to remake the franchise's older games in an aesthetic closer to modern Persona titles.

articles.title: Itch.io Reveals Just How Much AI Slop Is Flooding Gaming Storefronts
articles.summary: A quick glance at Steam or itch.io shows how gaming storefronts are flooded with new games as more developers use generative AI, making it harder than ever for indie devs with hand-crafted games to stand out.
body: As a gaming website and storefront, itch.io is positioned to be a very indie-friendly platform where almost anyone can sell or distribute the games they are working on. It's full of student-made and game jam projects, but many higher-profile indies are also available through itch.io and often given away in charity bundles. Because itch.io is already a very accessible and useful platform for indie developers, the new data it's shared is all the more concerning.

Late on Oct. 31, itch.io took to Bluesky to reveal that the number of game pages being created each day has doubled since Aug. 2026. According to the graph shared, the number of pages created per day was around 3,000 back then; now, that number is over 6,000 as of Oct. 30. Other replies from itch.io indicate that AI projects make up the majority of these new pages too.

articles.title: Footage of a Persona 1 remake has seemingly leaked online
articles.summary: Almost two minutes of footage from what appears to be a remake of the original Persona has leaked online.
body: The clip, which seemingly gives the remake the subtitle Be Your True Mind, was shared on the GamingLeaksAndRumours subreddit. It was uploaded to file-sharing site Gofile on 31st October under a Japanese filename that translates as "Megami Ibunroku Persona Remake".

Interestingly, the footage looks a lot like Atlus' more recent entries. It shows off stylish menus and a brief look at combat that closely resembles Persona 5 and Persona 3 Reload. There's also a short social link cutscene in a noticeably different, almost graphic novel art style.

Fans digging through the clip believe they have spotted several details that lend it credibility. These include what looks like Unreal Engine debug text in the top left corner during battle (Atlus switched to Unreal Engine for Persona 3 Reload), a new remix of the original PlayStation game's Pandora theme, and the protagonist being referred to as "Boy With Earring", which is how he is named in Persona 2: Eternal Punishment.
Atlus has not announced a Persona 1 remake, and we can't verify the footage, so treat all of this with the usual caveats.
points: Almost two minutes of footage from what appears to be a remake of the original Persona has leaked online.
It was uploaded to file-sharing site Gofile on 31st October under a Japanese filename that translates as "Megami Ibunroku Persona Remake".

articles.title: Composer and designer Lena Raine explains how Pigstep altered Minecraft's approach to music: 'The prompt I keep hearing is "Oh, Pigstep was such a banger that they want more bangers"'
articles.summary: Rick has been fascinated by PC gaming since he was seven years old, when he used to sneak into his dad's home office for covert sessions of Doom. He grew up on a diet of similarly unsuitable games, with favourites including Quake, Thief, Half-Life and Deus Ex.
body: Welcome to Disk Cleanup, our regular weekend feature delving into the PCs of PC gaming luminaries. Come back every weekend to read a new interview, digging into the important questions, like "How tidy is your desktop?" and "What game will you never uninstall?"

Lena Raine's formative gaming experience was playing Myst on a Mac Quadra 610, exploring Cyan Worlds' enigmatic island in parallel with her father: "We each had our own playthrough, so we were sending each other notes in the little journal that it came with," she says. "I still have the little book that we wrote in."

Raine always aspired to be a composer for video games, but she initially joined the industry as a games tester for Nintendo America, working several other testing jobs before being hired by ArenaNet as a game designer. While working on Guild Wars 2, Raine designed a bell-choir minigame for the MMO's Winter's Day Christmas update, including writing the music for it. "It was a bizarre first-step into game music," she says. "But that eventually led to at last some visibility for the other music I was writing."

articles.title: 'An absolute behemoth': Wildly ambitious FPS Selaco is getting a massive update that doubles its size and adds 'a heavy machinegun that fires literal explosions'
articles.summary: If you're a fan of first-person shooters and haven't played Selaco, you should. Built in the Doom engine and inspired by FEAR, Half-Life and System Shock, Selaco is a rollicking, dizzyingly ambitious sci-fi FPS where you battle a mercenary incursion of a vast, city-sized space station that's home…
body: Launched into Steam early access in 2024, Selaco's first chapter alone is as long as some entire '90s shooters. Now, developer Altered Orbit Studios is preparing to release an update that will not only double the length of the game, but also introduce a wide array of new features and rework much of its existing design.

Described by Altered Orbit as "an absolute behemoth", Selaco: The Machines of War introduces the second of a planned three chapters to the FPS. Chapter two comprises 19 new campaign maps, which apparently amounts to "6-8 hours of additional content". Alongside further story elements and a voice for the protagonist, the chapter also introduces what sounds like a persistent enemy, in the form of "an unstoppable machine" that is "hunting you down."

articles.title: Dune: Awakening's free Blood and Ice expansion swaps sand for snow on 1st December
articles.summary: Funcom's survival MMO Dune: Awakening is heading north with a free expansion that trades the deserts of Arrakis for a frozen new map.
body: The expansion, called Blood and Ice, will release on 1st December. Funcom said it adds "around 35 hours of new progression", along with new vehicle modules, augments, and specialisation traits. It's coming to PC, PS5, and Xbox.

The new map, called the Polar Sink, turns the game's usual survival loop upside down. Instead of protecting yourself from extreme heat, you'll need to find ways to stay warm, upgrading your gear with resources found only in the Polar Sink.

The map is split into two biomes, the tundra and the ice cap. You'll start in the tundra, where wealthy water shipper families have built lavish strongholds, before trying to get into the heavily guarded ice cap. Once you're in, you can harvest ice to cool your base equipment and speed up production.

According to Funcom, the expansion "brings the focus back to ground-level survival, with traversal, temperature management, and combat all playing important roles in your progression". The studio also said future updates will add more reasons to go back to the region.

articles.title: Chronicles: Medieval developer faces imminent closure after losing funding: 'What makes it hurt is how close we are. Early access is in reach'
articles.summary: Chronicles: Medieval is an impressive looking open-world sandbox where players explore a dynamic Medieval world and fight in massive, authentic battles. It's been in development for more than four years and is due to launch into Steam early access early in 2027.
body: However, there is a very real chance this will no longer happen, as developer Raw Power Games suddenly faces closure after funding for its game was pulled.

On Friday, Raw Power Games posted a statement to Steam and on social media channels (via IGN ), explaining how the studio has suddenly found itself in dire straits. "Due to circumstances outside our control, the necessary funding for Raw Power Games is no longer in place," the studio wrote. "Without it, we can't keep building Chronicles: Medieval, and right now the studio is at real risk of closing."

This appears to be a sudden development. Through October, the studio had been posting regular development updates, including an incredibly detailed deep dive on Medieval coats of arms and how they would appear in the game. None of it suggested a studio that's in trouble, so it seems this has caught Raw Power off guard.
points: Chronicles: Medieval is an impressive looking open-world sandbox where players explore a dynamic Medieval world and fight in massive, authentic battles.

articles.title: It's not just Steam: New game pages created per day on Itch.io have doubled in the last two months, with AI slop the likely culprit
articles.summary: Rick has been fascinated by PC gaming since he was seven years old, when he used to sneak into his dad's home office for covert sessions of Doom. He grew up on a diet of similarly unsuitable games, with favourites including Quake, Thief, Half-Life and Deus Ex.
body: It seems it isn't just Steam that's being flooded with AI slop. Indie games storefront itch.io has reported that the number of new game pages being created per day on the site has doubled in the past two months, and just like Valve's much bigger distribution service, the finger is being pointed at AI.

Over on Bluesky, itch.io shared an image of a bar chart labelled "game events". The chart shows that, between August 3 and October 30, the number of new game pages being created per day has risen from around 3,000 to regularly surpassing 6,000. It's a ratio that more or less matches the increase in Steam demos showcased at the most recent Next Fest, which rose from around 4,000 to over 8,000.

While Itch doesn't explicitly point the finger at AI as the cause, it heavily infers it. When Bluesky user Tommy's Homemade Games asked "Do you know why?" Itch responded "take a guess" followed by emojis of a crying face and a robot. Another Bluesky account, BardZaku, asked "is it AI dreck?" to which the account replied with an emoji of a face with bags under its eyes.
points: Rick has been fascinated by PC gaming since he was seven years old, when he used to sneak into his dad's home office for covert sessions of Doom.

There's not a whole lot of footage to actually look at, just shy of two minutes all told. One bit shows the game's protagonist walking through a school at night before starting a battle. articles.title: Pikmin 4 Nintendo Switch 2 Edition launches 12th November and a demo is out tomorrow
articles.summary: Pikmin 4 Nintendo Switch 2 Edition will launch on 12th November, bundled with a new mode called Dandori Academy.
body: Nintendo confirmed the date during yesterday's surprise Pikmin Day Direct, which also revealed that a demo will land on the Nintendo eShop on 2nd November. Any progress you make in the demo will transfer to the full game if you buy it.
Dandori Academy is a timed exam mode. The Direct showed off one of its exams, Gargantuan Garden, which challenges players to collect gold nuggets before time runs out ( thanks, Insider Gaming ).
The Switch 2 Edition will also let you give voice commands to Oatchi, the game’s dog companion. If you already own Pikmin 4 on the original Switch, you can buy an upgrade pack from the eShop.

Nintendo had warned ahead of the broadcast that there would be no new game announcements. Instead, Shigeru Miyamoto introduced Japanese actor Fuka Koshiba as a new ambassador for the series, and Nintendo confirmed that 1st November, today, is now Pikmin Day.
